question: A square with side length \(x\) is inscribed in a right triangle with sides of length \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) so that one vertex of the square coincides with the right-angle vertex of the triangle. A square with side length \(y\) is inscribed in another right triangle with sides of length \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) so that one side of the square lies on the hypotenuse of the triangle. What is \(\dfrac{x}{y}?\)
solution:
The square sides create smaller right triangles similar to the original triangle. These similarities let us express the needed lengths in terms of the square side.

Label the first triangle \(ABC\), with right angle at \(A\), \(AB=3\), and \(AC=4\). Name the square \(APQR\) in order, with \(P\) on \(AB\), \(R\) on \(AC\), and \(Q\) on \(BC\). Its sides all have length \(x\), so
\[
BP=3-x,\qquad RC=4-x.
\]
The right triangles \(BPQ\) and \(QRC\) are similar: their right angles are at \(P\) and \(R\), and \(\angle PBQ=\angle RQC\) because \(BP\parallel QR\). Corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{x}{3-x}=\frac{4-x}{x}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
x^2=(3-x)(4-x)=12-7x+x^2,
\qquad x=\frac{12}{7}.
\]

In the second triangle, again use \(AB=3\), \(AC=4\), and \(BC=5\), with right angle at \(A\). Name the square \(DEFG\) in order, with \(D,E\) on \(BC\) in that order from \(B\) to \(C\), \(G\) on \(AB\), and \(F\) on \(AC\).

Since \(GF\parallel BC\), triangles \(AGF\) and \(ABC\) are similar. Thus
\[
\frac{AG}{3}=\frac{GF}{5}=\frac{y}{5},
\qquad AG=\frac35y.
\]
Triangle \(BDG\) is right at \(D\) and shares angle \(B\) with the original triangle, so it too is similar to the original. Here \(DG\) corresponds to the leg of length 4, while \(BG\) corresponds to the hypotenuse. Hence
\[
\frac{BG}{5}=\frac{DG}{4}=\frac{y}{4},
\qquad BG=\frac54y.
\]
Since \(AG+GB=AB=3\),
\[
\left(\frac35+\frac54\right)y=3,
\qquad \frac{37}{20}y=3,
\qquad y=\frac{60}{37}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{x}{y}=\frac{12}{7}\cdot\frac{37}{60}
=\boxed{\frac{37}{35}}.
\]
The answer is D.
